sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Yellow toadflax is a rhizomatous perennial 20–80 cm tall, native to Eurasia and introduced in North America. It grows in open, dry to moderately moist places and can form colonies.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: Its leaves are narrow and linear. The yellow, two-lipped flowers have an orange palate and a long spur; the corolla is about 1–1.5 cm long excluding the spur, which is itself about 1–1.5 cm long. The ovoid capsule releases flattened, winged seeds.

sections.title: Toxicity
sections.text: The plant contains a toxic glycoside and can poison livestock when eaten in large amounts, although it is unpalatable. No safe food use is established.
